lessons.sourceTitleEnglish: Teach a Friend How a Madrid Bar Breakfast Works
lessons.sourceObjectiveEnglish: Explain step by step how to order, eat and pay at a Madrid bar counter, then have a friend explain it back.
lessons.sourceSpeakingEnglish: You are coaching the AI, Brazilian traveler Thiago, through a Madrid bar breakfast: explain ordering, eating and paying in order with primero, luego, después, porque and por eso, then ask him to explain the routine back to you.
lessons.sourceGrammarFocusEnglish: Connectors for sequence and cause (primero pides en la barra, luego te sirven, porque pagas al final, por eso guardas el tique)

sourceWordsEnglish.en: the gap (free spot at the bar)
First you find a spot at the bar, and then you order.
Don't wait for a table, because almost everyone here eats breakfast standing up.
You pay at the end, so don't throw away the receipt.
One moment, please, he's still deciding.
I'll have a black coffee and some porras, please.
Afterwards, when you finish, you ask the waiter for the bill.
Okay, now you explain it to me, step by step.
Can you ring me up when you get a chance?

sourcePassageEnglish: Emma and her Brazilian friend Thiago walk into a bar in Lavapiés to have breakfast before strolling around the neighborhood.
It's really hectic, because at 9 half the neighborhood has its coffee at the bar.
Emma: First you find a spot at the bar, and then you order.
Emma: Don't wait for a table, because almost everyone here eats breakfast standing up.
Thiago finds a spot at the end of the bar and leaves his backpack on a free bar stool.
Emma: Before ordering, you look at the chalkboard menu, because that's where they write the day's prices.
The breakfast deal includes a coffee and churros for 3 euros.
Suddenly Paco, the waiter, plants himself in front of them and asks: What can I get you?
Thiago freezes, so Emma answers: One moment, please, he's still deciding.
After looking at the chalkboard again, Thiago says: I'll have a black coffee and some porras, please.
Emma orders a slice of Spanish omelette and a fresh-squeezed orange juice, and Paco serves them right away.
When Paco puts down the plates, he also puts a small receipt under Thiago's cup.
Emma: You pay at the end, so don't throw away the receipt.
Emma: Afterwards, when you finish, you ask the waiter for the bill.
Emma: If you pay by card, Paco brings you the card reader, and if you pay cash, he gives you your change.
Emma: Tipping isn't required, but if you want, you leave a few coins from your change in the tip jar.
Emma: Okay, now you explain it to me, step by step.
Thiago: First I find a spot and order, then I eat breakfast standing up, and since I pay at the end, I keep the receipt.

lessons.objectiveFrenchCourseEnglish: Montrer à un ami comment lire le menu, commander et vérifier le paiement dans un café parisien.
lessons.focusEnglish: Sequence and cause: first we read the menu, then we order; because payment varies, we ask when to pay.
lessons.focusFrench: Connecteurs de suite et de cause : d’abord on lit la carte, puis on commande ; comme le paiement varie, on demande quand payer.
lessons.teachingNotesEnglish: This is a fictional café. Do not generalize standing service, payment order, tips, prices or receipts to all Paris cafés.

english: Emma and her friend Thiago enter a neighborhood café in Paris.
Thiago wants to practice ordering breakfast in French.
Emma suggests reading the menu board before approaching the counter.
They see a breakfast special with a hot drink and a pastry.
Thiago asks whether an empty stool is available.
The server says they may sit there.
Emma explains that service and payment can vary by café.
She asks the server when this café takes payment.
The server says they can pay at the counter after ordering.
Thiago hesitates, so Emma asks for a moment.
Then Thiago orders an espresso and a croissant.
Emma orders a tartine and fresh orange juice.
The server repeats the order to check it.
Thiago asks whether he may pay by card.
The server brings the card reader and gives him a receipt.
Emma asks Thiago to explain what they did, step by step.
Thiago says they read the menu, checked the seat, ordered and paid.
Emma smiles because he can now describe this café’s routine himself.
french: Emma et son ami Thiago entrent dans un café de quartier à Paris.
Thiago veut s’entraîner à commander son petit-déjeuner en français.
Emma propose de lire l’ardoise avant de s’approcher du comptoir.
Ils voient une formule petit-déjeuner avec une boisson chaude et une viennoiserie.
Thiago demande si un tabouret libre est disponible.
Le serveur dit qu’ils peuvent s’y asseoir.
Emma explique que le service et le paiement peuvent varier selon le café.
Elle demande au serveur quand on paie dans ce café.
Le serveur dit qu’ils peuvent payer au comptoir après avoir commandé.
Thiago hésite ; Emma demande donc un instant.
Puis Thiago commande un expresso et un croissant.
Emma commande une tartine et un jus d’orange pressé.
Le serveur répète la commande pour la vérifier.
Thiago demande s’il peut payer par carte.
Le serveur apporte le terminal de paiement et lui remet un ticket de caisse.
Emma demande à Thiago d’expliquer ce qu’ils ont fait, étape par étape.
Thiago dit qu’ils ont lu l’ardoise, vérifié la place, commandé et payé.
Emma sourit, car il peut maintenant décrire lui-même le fonctionnement de ce café.

lessons.sourceTitleEnglish: Explain Media or Entera at a Seville Tostada Bar
lessons.sourceObjectiveEnglish: Explain how tostadas are ordered by bread type, size and topping, and why locals choose each one.
lessons.sourceSpeakingEnglish: You are explaining Seville's tostada system to the AI, hostel roommate Ingrid: walk her through bread type, size and toppings and why locals choose each, using impersonal se (se pide media o entera) and si + present (si pides mollete…).
lessons.sourceGrammarFocusEnglish: Impersonal se; si + present for general truths (se pide media o entera; si pides mollete, te lo tuestan)

Excuse me, is the house bread a mollete or a Vienna roll?

sourcePassageEnglish: This morning, at a tostada bar in Triana, I explain to Ingrid how tostadas are ordered in Seville.
Me: Here you order the bread first and then the topping.
Me: Here you order a half or a whole, depending on how hungry you are.
Me: If you're really hungry, order a whole one.
Me: If you order a mollete, the bread stays soft inside, because it has a lot of soft crumb.
Me: The Vienna roll has a thinner, crunchier crust, and a lot of people prefer it for that reason.
Me: If you order a pitufo, they bring you a smaller roll, perfect to go with a coffee.
Me: I think the house bread is a mollete, but I'm going to ask.
I say to the owner: Excuse me, is the house bread a mollete or a Vienna roll?
Rocío: The house bread is a Vienna roll, and the mollete is ordered separately.
Me: Thanks for correcting me, I didn't know that.
Then I tell Ingrid that the most typical choice is grated tomato with a good drizzle of olive oil, because it is light and fresh.
Me: Manteca colorá is pork lard with paprika, and zurrapa de lomo has little pieces of pork loin in lard.
Ingrid tells me she doesn't eat pork, and I explain that cured ham is pork too.
Me: If you don't eat pork, avoid the manteca colorá and the zurrapa.
Ingrid: How do you order it here if I want it lightly toasted?
Rocío: You order it with light toasting, and we bring it out to you softer.
In the end, Ingrid orders a half with tomato and oil, lightly toasted, and Rocío leaves the salt shaker on the table for her.

lessons.titleFrenchCourseEnglish: Expliquer les choix d’une boulangerie lyonnaise
lessons.objectiveFrenchCourseEnglish: Expliquer la taille du pain, les garnitures et les ingrédients à vérifier avant de commander.
lessons.focusEnglish: Impersonal on and if-clauses: here we choose the bread first; if you want a small portion, ask what sizes are offered.
lessons.focusFrench: On impersonnel et propositions en si : ici, on choisit d’abord le pain ; si tu veux une petite portion, demande quelles tailles sont proposées.
lessons.teachingNotesEnglish: Do not import Seville mollete/pitufo/manteca customs. Lyon scene is fictional; the baker confirms actual sizes, availability and ingredients.

passage.titleFrench: Expliquer les choix d’une boulangerie lyonnaise
english: In a Lyon bakery, Camille explains the breakfast choices to her friend Ingrid.
They look at the breads, pastries and toppings on the menu.
Camille says they should ask which portions are available today.
The baker says the café has small rolls and slices of house bread.
Ingrid asks whether the house bread is a baguette.
The baker explains that today it is a round loaf.
Camille thanks her for clarifying instead of guessing.
Ingrid asks which bread has a soft crumb and which has a crisp crust.
The baker describes the breads available that morning.
Camille explains that Ingrid can choose butter, jam or cheese as a topping.
Ingrid says she does not eat pork.
Camille points out the ham option but asks the baker about other ingredients too.
The baker checks the current ingredient list with them.
Ingrid asks for a small bread with jam.
She asks whether it can be toasted lightly.
The baker confirms what the kitchen can prepare.
Camille summarizes the choices: bread, portion, topping and preparation.
Ingrid repeats her order clearly to the baker.
french: Dans une boulangerie lyonnaise, Camille explique les choix du petit-déjeuner à son amie Ingrid.
Elles regardent les pains, les viennoiseries et les garnitures sur la carte.
Camille dit qu’elles devraient demander quelles portions sont proposées aujourd’hui.
La boulangère dit que le café propose des petits pains et des tranches de pain maison.
Ingrid demande si le pain maison est une baguette.
La boulangère explique qu’aujourd’hui, c’est une miche.
Camille la remercie pour la précision au lieu de deviner.
Ingrid demande quel pain a une mie moelleuse et lequel a une croûte croustillante.
La boulangère décrit les pains disponibles ce matin-là.
Camille explique qu’Ingrid peut choisir du beurre, de la confiture ou du fromage comme garniture.
Ingrid dit qu’elle ne mange pas de porc.
Camille montre l’option au jambon, mais demande aussi à la boulangère des précisions sur les autres ingrédients.
La boulangère vérifie avec elles la liste actuelle des ingrédients.
Ingrid demande un petit pain avec de la confiture.
Elle demande s’il peut être grillé légèrement.
La boulangère confirme ce que la cuisine peut préparer.
Camille résume les choix : le pain, la portion, la garniture et la préparation.
Ingrid répète clairement sa commande à la boulangère.

lessons.sourceTitleEnglish: Coach Your Niece to Order Café de Olla Alone
lessons.sourceObjectiveEnglish: Coach a teenager to order café de olla and a pan dulce on her own, with clear tips about the hot clay cup.
lessons.sourceSpeakingEnglish: You are the aunt or uncle, and the AI is your 15-year-old niece Sofi: coach her to order café de olla and a pan dulce on her own, using commands with pronouns like pídelo, agárralo por el asa and no lo toques todavía.
lessons.sourceGrammarFocusEnglish: Commands with object pronouns (pídelo sin piloncillo, agárralo por el asa, no lo toques todavía)

sourceWordsEnglish.en: the hot chocolate made with water
Order it without piloncillo if you don't want it so sweet.
Hold it by the handle, never by the rim.
Don't touch it yet; wait until it stops steaming.
Taste it slowly, because the clay holds the heat.
Greet her first and speak to her formally.
Ask her how much it is and pay her with the 50-peso bill.
Good morning, doña Eustolia, may I have a café de olla?
You've got this, I'll wait for you here on the bench.

sourcePassageEnglish: Aunt Carmen and her niece Sofi, 15 years old, arrive early at a small eatery in the Oaxaca market.
Doña Eustolia's stall is at the back, and she serves the café de olla very hot in a clay mug.
Carmen wants Sofi to order alone for the first time, so she coaches her on the eatery's bench.
Carmen: Greet her first and speak to her formally.
Carmen: Say it like this: Good morning, doña Eustolia, may I have a café de olla?
Sofi asks if the coffee is very sweet, and Carmen explains that doña Eustolia makes it with piloncillo and cinnamon.
Carmen: Order it without piloncillo if you don't want it so sweet.
Carmen: If you'd rather have something else, order a hot chocolate made with water, which is also really good.
Carmen: Pick a pan de yema and ask doña Eustolia for it with the coffee.
Carmen: Ask her how much it is and pay her with the 50-peso bill.
Carmen: If she gives you coins as change, put them away in your pants pocket.
Carmen: Hold it by the handle, never by the rim.
Carmen: Don't touch it yet; wait until it stops steaming.
Carmen: If it's still very hot, leave it on the table until it's lukewarm.
Carmen: Taste it slowly, because the clay holds the heat.
Carmen: You've got this, I'll wait for you here on the bench.
Sofi walks to the stall alone, greets doña Eustolia and orders her café de olla with her pan de yema.
Minutes later, Sofi comes back to the bench holding the mug firmly by the handle, with her bread in her other hand.

sourceVerbsEnglish.exampleEnglish: Order it without piloncillo if you don't want it so sweet.

sourceGrammarExamplesEnglish: If it's very hot, leave it on the table for a little while.

english: In Montréal, Carmen takes her teenage niece Sofie to a café for breakfast.
Sofie wants to order a hot chocolate and a pastry by herself.
Carmen waits at a nearby table and helps her prepare a polite request.
She tells Sofie to greet the server first.
Sofie asks how much the hot chocolate costs.
The server points to the price on the menu.
Carmen says Sofie can ask for no extra sugar if she prefers.
Sofie chooses a pastry and checks its price too.
Then she walks to the counter and greets the server.
She asks for a hot chocolate and the pastry.
The server repeats the order and places the cup on the counter.
Sofie sees steam rising and leaves the cup where it is.
She asks the server whether the drink is still very hot.
Carmen tells her to wait before drinking if she is unsure.
Sofie pays after the server confirms the total.
She brings the pastry back to the table while the drink stays on the counter.
Carmen praises her clear request and asks her to explain what she said.
Sofie repeats her order and says she will wait before drinking.
french: À Montréal, Carmen emmène sa nièce adolescente Sofie dans un café pour le petit-déjeuner.
Sofie veut commander elle-même un chocolat chaud et une viennoiserie.
Carmen attend à une table voisine et l’aide à préparer une demande polie.
Elle dit à Sofie de saluer d’abord le serveur.
Sofie demande combien coûte le chocolat chaud.
Le serveur lui montre le prix sur la carte.
Carmen dit que Sofie peut demander sans sucre ajouté si elle préfère.
Sofie choisit une viennoiserie et vérifie aussi son prix.
Puis elle va au comptoir et salue le serveur.
Elle demande un chocolat chaud et la viennoiserie.
Le serveur répète la commande et pose la tasse sur le comptoir.
Sofie voit de la vapeur s’élever et laisse la tasse où elle est.
Elle demande au serveur si la boisson est encore très chaude.
Carmen lui dit d’attendre avant de boire si elle n’est pas sûre.
Sofie paie après que le serveur a confirmé le total.
Elle rapporte la viennoiserie à la table tandis que la boisson reste au comptoir.
Carmen la félicite pour sa demande claire et lui demande d’expliquer ce qu’elle a dit.
Sofie répète sa commande et dit qu’elle attendra avant de boire.
